r3-a05.reason: A feminine noun phrase that is dative-or-genitive by its form (meiner Schwester) is left open after a verb that takes the dative (gehören).

r3-a11.reason: je … desto is not recognised when the comparatives are not ones the detector knows (länger, nervöser).

r3-a14.reason: A genitive attribute after its noun (die Häuser der Stadt) is left dative-or-genitive. The participle of an -ieren verb that is not in the word list (renoviert) is guessed as a finite form of an invented infinitive (renoviern), so the passive is not recorded.

r3-k01.reason: A participle that ends its clause without an auxiliary (fand er sich … verwandelt) is read as a finite verb; the als-clause that opens the sentence is not recorded as verb-final.

r3-k05.reason: An adjectival noun after andere (Andere Reisende) is read as feminine singular although the verb is plural. Haremsfrauen: Harem is not in the word list, so the compound is not taken apart and the unknown plural keeps its plural spelling as its lemma.

r3-k07.reason: The question word wer as subject does not fix the verb's person (weiß stays 1st-or-3rd).

r3-k08.reason: Pult is not in the word list: its gender is honestly left masculine-or-neuter after vom.

r3-k11.reason: A stranded prefix whose joined verb is not in the word list (glitt … zurück = zurückgleiten) is not joined into a unit.

r3-k13.reason: In a long sentence with a comma-separated adjective list inside the als-clause, the clause is not delimited: its subject does not fix begann, the clause is not recorded as verb-final, and ließ … ab (ablassen) before the comma is not joined.
